summary: GET one https url and write the bytes to the output, optionally only its first N seconds. The host must be one the ops pack names; the url is checked again on every redirect hop.

parity.note: The whole-file path writes the origin's bytes verbatim, so it is bit_exact by construction. The windowed path is an ffmpeg `-c copy` remux — no re-encode, no scaler, no rate control — and is deterministic for a fixed ffmpeg build, the same condition media.scale states: the pinned BUILD, not the box. tests/test_op_media_fetch.py asserts the argv is a pure function of (url, path, seconds), so a drift shows as an argv diff in milliseconds rather than as different bytes after a fetch. FAILURE: `dst` is OPTIONAL — a dead origin leaves no file instead of raising, because one chain carries a whole batch of candidates and a raising handler would let one dead url kill every sibling. The CALLER decides whether a missing file is fatal: fetch_broll.fetch_clip raises for a master, the rank lane tops the row up.

url.description: The ORIGIN to fetch. A LOCATION, never a decision: it carries no threshold and no editorial rule, and this op has no vocabulary for what the bytes are for. It is a param rather than an input binding so that the host allowlist can live in the ops pack, at the one place a third-party url is dereferenced — an input url is fetched by the runner before any handler exists, which would push the check into podagent/cp.py (submodule commit, image rebuild) and hide `needs: [net]` from the placement gate. The brain refuses to bind a credential-carrying url (op_backend.assert_bindable_origin); the pod refuses to fetch an unlisted host (montyops.stock_hosts). Both, on purpose.

prefix_seconds.description: Pull only [0, N] of the file. A BYTE WINDOW on the file's own axis — a PREFIX, never a mid-clip seek and never a choice of moment, so it cannot disclose where in a clip anything is cut. Omit for the whole file. Measured on both keyed providers: ftyp+moov sit at the front and the CDNs serve Range, so a pexels 4K/57s master costs 12.6 MB for 5 s instead of 137.3 MB.
